about: In-app news ('소식', Docs/InAppNews.md): which feed the app reads, which items it lists, which one becomes the one-time card, what it remembers — the same vectors for the Mac · iPhone · iPad (SpiraldayKit) and Windows · Android (web). The private repo's web/tests/fixtures/news-rules.json is the same bytes as this file (Tests/Fixtures/news-rules.json). Reference implementation: Scripts/news-check.mjs (open · list · markListSeen; node Scripts/news-check.mjs --fixtures). Owner decision 2026-10-11: no accounts, no push — a static feed on spiralday.com and notes bundled with the app.

conventions.feed: parse · select: 'feed' is the JSON the server sends (serialize it with any JSON writer, then hand the BYTES to the parser), or the name of one in 'feeds', or null (nothing cached). 'feedText' is the exact text instead (UTF-8), 'feedBase64' the exact bytes. 'bom': true puts EF BB BF in front. 'padToBytes': n appends ASCII spaces until the body is n bytes.
conventions.repeat: {"$repeat": "s", "times": n} in a string's place is s repeated n times. In the items array, {"$repeat": {item}, "times": n} is n copies of the item whose ids get -1 … -n appended. Expand both before serializing.
conventions.parseExpect: accepted: whether the whole feed is read (false = keep the previous cache). ids: the items kept, in feed order. links (when given): each kept item's link after the allowlist (null = no link).
conventions.select: One app open (open() in the spec): env and state are merged over selectDefaults; bundled is the name of a whats-new.json in 'bundled' (default selectDefaults.bundled). expect.card: null | {type:'notice', id} | {type:'whatsNew', app}. expect.save: the state the app stores right after this open (a card counts as seen the moment it shows). expect.list · dot: Settings › 소식 (list() in the spec) computed from expect.save — title · body in env.lang ('ko'; anything else is 'en', each text falling back to ko on its own), unseen = that row's dot, dot = any unseen. Then opening the list adds every listed id to seen, after which dot is false — check that too.
conventions.text: Lengths are Unicode code points (Swift unicodeScalars.count, JS [...s].length) — not UTF-16 units, not grapheme clusters.
conventions.patterns: All patterns are ASCII only and match the whole string: no \d (Swift's matches other digits), and a final line break does not match ($ in ICU · Swift may match before it).
conventions.dates: dates · versions.valid · links: [value, ok]. A value that is not a string is never ok. versions.compare: [a, b, sign of a − b].
conventions.fetch: status null = timeout or no connection. body: valid = a feed the parser accepts, invalid = one it rejects, tooBig = more than limits.maxBytes. replace = store this body (and its ETag · Last-Modified) as the cache; keep = the previous cache stays as it is.

parse.name: the smallest feed (what site/news/news.json starts as)
unknown fields are ignored, at the top and in items
version 2 is not read (a new format gets a new URL)
version true (Swift: an NSNumber bool is not 1)
a lone surrogate anywhere, even in an unknown field
a surrogate pair escape is one character
a duplicated key: the value it overwrites counts too — a lone surrogate there and the file is not read (JSON.parse keeps only the later value)
a duplicated key whose overwritten value nests 17 deep: not read
only the first 50 items are read
entries that are not objects are skipped
duplicate ids: the first VALID one wins
titles: ko needed, en optional, one line, 80 code points
bodies: line breaks are \n only, 600 code points
minVersion · maxVersion: every value must be a version, unknown keys too
syncOnly is a boolean (Swift: an NSNumber 1 is not true)
a link off the allowlist is removed, the item stays
